Asserted across all tracked markdown, HTML visualizer, JSON datasets, and benchmark docs by scripts/check_docs_hygiene.py and crates/expanse/tests/test_visualizer_sync.rs.

figures.replacement: single thread only: get_many 1.152x [1.040, 1.227] and per-call get 0.656x [0.637, 0.691] against the dict control (results/baseline_python_concurrency.json); at two threads and above the control is multi-modal and the comparison is INTERMEDIATE
figures.rationale: bindings/python/bench_concurrency.py built its miss half as `k ^ (1 << 63)` of each hit (AGENTS.md §8.6 degenerate miss shape) and alternated hits and misses strictly. The defect is present in every arm but not equal in magnitude across them: a hash `dict` has no descent depth for the miss shape to distort and the trie does, so every cross-arm figure from that run is not a like-for-like comparison. Within-arm scaling was retained at the time on the reasoning that the contamination was constant along the thread axis; #774 refuted that for a second, independent reason -- the run was also unpinned, and pin exposure grows with thread count -- so the scaling curve was superseded too.

figures.replacement: 47.84 B/key allocator and 42.77 B/key mem_used on `short` at 10^6, 41.33 / 37.71 on `skewed`, 63.45 / 54.77 on `prefixed`, 47.83 / 46.78 on `beyond`, and 115,916 allocations per 100,000 `short` keys (63.97 -> 42.48 B/key on the HOT gate), all at 41dc7bfd after #723 (docs/benchmarks/masstree_comparison/results/baseline_string_memory.json, docs/benchmarks/hot_comparison/results/baseline_string_memory.json, docs/benchmarks/hot_comparison/results/string_validate.log)
figures.rationale: The 2ce92b7f string artifacts were measured against an `ExpanseStrMap` leaf that spent two allocations on every key not resolved inside a terminal chunk — a `StrSuffix` shell plus a separate byte buffer. #723 made the leaf a single allocation and the whole string sweep was re-measured on the reference host at 41dc7bfd; `counter` is unchanged in both instruments because it allocates no suffix leaf. Superseded, not silently overwritten (§8.7).

figures.replacement: scan cells re-measured at 7fe02c0b through `ExpanseStrMap::cursor_at_or_after` (#722): masstree 0.089 [0.089, 0.091] at worst and 2.149 [2.140, 2.175] at best, Expanse winning 3 of 36; HOT still winning 72 of 72 but every cell moved 1.38x-11.21x. Paired against the positional surface at 82f400b0 (docs/benchmarks/masstree_comparison/results/baseline_string_latency.json, docs/benchmarks/hot_comparison/results/baseline_string_latency.json)
figures.rationale: The string scan pillars measured `next_at_or_after` / `next_after` — a fresh root descent per element that allocated a key the arm discarded — against competitor visitors that never materialize a key (Masstree's `str_scan`) or that are already incremental (HOT's `lower_bound` plus iterator). That is a section 8.3 asymmetry, and #722 gave ExpanseStrMap a cursor and re-paired both arms. Superseded, not silently overwritten (section 8.7). `0.019` is deliberately not a pattern here: it is also the sixteen-writer concurrent ratio, and a figure that means two things cannot be gated on its digits alone.

figures.replacement: 0.124 at 16 threads and 0.121 at 8, measured under the P-core pin (results/baseline_python_concurrency.json)
figures.rationale: results/baseline_python_concurrency.json was measured unpinned on a hybrid host and scripts/bench_pin.sh was never sourced by this harness. Pin exposure is not constant along the thread axis -- 0.999 [0.927, 1.040] at one thread against 5.569 [5.305, 5.742] at sixteen -- so the within-arm scaling curve, which normalises every width by its own single-thread arm, is distorted most exactly where it makes its claim. The unpinned 16-thread cell reproduces at 0.121 Mops/s, which is what identified the committed run as unpinned. `0.019` is deliberately not a pattern: the sixteen-writer concurrent ratio is the same digits, and this entry's context words are generic enough to match near that table.

figures.rationale: HOT-ROWEX concurrent figures from the two runs at 6f8d6ba5, which precedes #997 (deferred-gated allocator shards and padded writer state promoted to the default) and #1010. Every cell on a write path was stale (AGENTS.md section 8.7). At 929574b5 all 14 writer cells at W >= 2 moved up in both runs, each new interval clear of both earlier ones, and Expanse wins every writer cell through eight writers on both arms where ROWEX previously won from four; no reader cell and no single-writer cell moved. The two pairs are separate runs at two commits, so the movement is attributed to no single change.

figures.replacement: docs/benchmarks/masstree_comparison/README.md section 7 (corrections in sections 1 and 2): results/baseline_concurrent.json and results/baseline_concurrent_run2.json, two runs at 929574b5 under pin 0-15 (table P: the per-core pair); the retired pair is kept at results/at_6f8d6ba5/
figures.rationale: Masstree concurrent figures from the two runs at 6f8d6ba5, which precedes #997, #1001 (the per-node optimistic write path for SyncExpanseStrMap, whose writers serialised until then) and #1010. At 929574b5 every writer-only cell at W >= 2 moved up on both arms in both runs (eight string writers 1.89-2.02 to 18.39-18.55 M inserts/s), the four string reader cells under writers went from Masstree's (0.045-0.281) to Expanse's (1.189-1.299), and the string health cells' restart share went from 62-93% of walks to 0.01-0.07%. The string single writer's pooled median fell 3.66-3.88 to 2.79-2.83 M inserts/s; that difference is not a measured regression, because the earlier cell was bimodal by round order (3.00 timed first, 4.11 timed second) and its median described neither mode.
